events.name: Sample Hack 2026
events.tagline: 72 hours. One spec. Judged by the platform you build.
events.description: Sample Hack 2026 is a 72-hour online sprint for builders of developer tools, applied AI and civic technology. Teams of one to four ship a working project, submit before the hard UTC deadline and are judged by a panel using a weighted rubric. Scores are normalized across judges so a strict judge cannot sink a project and a generous one cannot float it.
events.rules:
1. Teams of 1–4. One team per person.
2. All code must be written during the event and published under an OSI-approved licence.
3. The submission deadline is enforced by the server clock in UTC. There are no late submissions.
4. Judges score against the published rubric; conflicts of interest are declared and excluded.
5. Community voting is open to everyone; automated or duplicate votes are flagged and not counted.

submission.title: Deadline Sentinel
submission.tagline: A server-clock-true countdown you can embed anywhere
submission.description: Deadline Sentinel is a tiny widget and CLI that shows the authoritative server-side time to every participant, flags client clock drift, and posts a warning to the team channel an hour before cutoff. It never trusts the browser clock.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Clock drift detection without NTP: we estimate offset from round-trip timing to the portal.

submission.title: Schema Scout
submission.tagline: Visual, reviewable Postgres schema diffs
submission.description: Schema Scout renders two database schemas side by side, highlights breaking changes (dropped columns, narrowed types, missing indexes) and generates a reversible migration plan with a risk score.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Detecting renames versus drop-and-add without false positives.

submission.title: Flaky Hunter
submission.tagline: Finds and quarantines flaky tests before they waste your CI minutes
submission.description: Flaky Hunter replays your test suite under controlled randomness (seed, ordering, timing) and uses Bayesian failure-rate estimates to separate flaky tests from real regressions.

submission.title: Offline Docs
submission.tagline: Instant full-text search across your dependencies' docs, no network
submission.description: Offline Docs indexes the documentation of every package in your lockfile into a 20 MB local index and serves sub-10ms search in the terminal and editor.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Fitting a BM25 index with typo tolerance into a small memory budget.

submission.title: Commit Coach
submission.tagline: Commit message feedback that actually teaches
submission.description: Commit Coach reviews staged changes and suggests a conventional-commit message, explaining each suggestion so junior developers learn the convention rather than copy it.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Summarising large diffs without a language model.

submission.title: Lock Radar
submission.tagline: Visualise lock contention in production Postgres
submission.description: Lock Radar samples pg_locks and pg_stat_activity to build a live wait-for graph, spotting deadlock cycles and the queries that cause them.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Sampling often enough to catch short waits without adding load.

submission.title: Whisper Notes
submission.tagline: On-device meeting transcription and action items
submission.description: Whisper Notes runs a quantised speech model locally, diarises speakers and extracts action items, so sensitive meetings never leave the laptop.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Real-time diarisation on a CPU-only laptop.

submission.title: Tiny Tutor
submission.tagline: A patient maths tutor that works on a 2 GB phone, offline
submission.description: Tiny Tutor pairs a small local language model with a curriculum graph so students in low-bandwidth regions get step-by-step hints instead of answers.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Keeping a 1B-parameter model responsive on low-end Android devices.

submission.title: Alt-Text Lens
submission.tagline: Meaningful image descriptions for screen-reader users
submission.description: Alt-Text Lens generates context-aware alt text for images in documents and flags decorative images, with a review queue for editors.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Evaluating description quality with blind and low-vision testers.

submission.title: Guardrail Bench
submission.tagline: A reproducible benchmark for prompt-injection defences
submission.description: Guardrail Bench ships 1,200 adversarial cases and a harness that scores guardrail libraries on precision, recall and latency, fully offline.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Writing attacks that generalise instead of overfitting to one model.

submission.title: Crop Doctor
submission.tagline: Plant disease detection from a phone photo, no signal needed
submission.description: Crop Doctor classifies 38 crop diseases on-device and recommends locally available treatments, designed with smallholder farmers.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Collecting field photos that match real lighting conditions.

submission.title: Ward Watch
submission.tagline: Residents report, the council responds, everyone sees the SLA
submission.description: Ward Watch is a municipal issue tracker with public response-time dashboards and duplicate report merging, deployable on a single council server.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Merging duplicate reports by location and description similarity.

submission.title: Transit Pulse
submission.tagline: Crowd-sourced bus reliability for cities without open data
submission.description: Transit Pulse lets riders tap when a bus arrives and turns those taps into reliability scores per route and stop, with privacy-preserving aggregation.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Making aggregated data useful without exposing individual trips.

submission.title: Budget Lens
submission.tagline: Explore your city's budget like a map
submission.description: Budget Lens turns council budget PDFs into an explorable treemap with year-over-year diffs and plain-language explanations.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Extracting tables reliably from inconsistent PDF layouts.

submission.title: FloodNet
submission.tagline: LoRa mesh flood alerts that work when the grid is down
submission.description: FloodNet uses cheap LoRa river sensors and a mesh of solar relays to push flood warnings to villages downstream, with no dependence on cellular networks.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Keeping relays alive through a week of monsoon cloud cover.

submission.title: Clinic Queue
submission.tagline: Fair, SMS-free queueing for walk-in clinics
submission.description: Clinic Queue gives patients a paper ticket with a QR code and shows a live queue on a TV, so no one waits outside and priority cases are visible to staff.

answers.qst_01_hardest: Designing for clinics with one shared computer and unreliable power.
